key_insight: Introduce a unified spatio-temporal token scoring mechanism that selects and prunes uninformative vision tokens across space and time, enabling efficient video vision-language models without sacrificing downstream VLM performance.
problem_solved: Reduces computational cost and latency in video VLMs by removing redundant visual tokens across frames while preserving the semantics needed for vision–language tasks—addressing limits of approaches that prune only within ViT or only within the LLM.
method: Compute unified importance scores for tokens that capture both spatial and temporal relevance across video frames.
Prune low-importance tokens before cross-modal fusion so the VLM processes fewer, more informative tokens.
Train or fine-tune scoring/pruning jointly with downstream VLM objectives to preserve task-specific accuracy while reducing compute.
impact: Makes video-capable VLMs substantially more efficient and deployable (lower latency, less compute/cost) for real-world tasks like captioning, retrieval, and question answering over video, with minimal performance loss.
visual_elements: Pipeline diagram: video frames → ViT → unified spatio-temporal token scorer → pruned tokens → VLM/LLM
Frame-level visualization: original tokens vs. retained tokens highlighted over several time steps
Bar chart: compute (FLOPs/latency) vs. accuracy trade-off comparing baseline VLM, ViT-only pruning, LLM-only pruning, and unified scoring
Icon grid: benefits (speed, cost, accuracy retention, scalability) with short captions
paper_title: Unified Spatio-Temporal Token Scoring for Efficient Video VLMs
paper_authors: Jianrui Zhang, Yue Yang, Rohun Tripathi, Winson Han, Ranjay Krishna
